question: Should ClawHub/OpenClaw support the legacy `curl -fsSL https://molt.bot/install.sh | zsh` install path, or should it be treated as retired in favor of the current `openclaw.ai` bash installer and ClawHub/OpenClaw install commands?
rationale: The failing helper is absent from current ClawHub source, while the live hosted URL now redirects to a separate OpenClaw installer, so automation cannot choose the support boundary or ownership model safely.

options.title: Retire or redirect legacy zsh usage
options.body: Point `molt.bot` users to `https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash` and current ClawHub/OpenClaw install docs, then treat zsh-piped legacy failures as unsupported.

options.title: Own and harden the hosted installer
options.body: Track the installer source, reproduce the Homebrew/zsh cleanup failure, and add regression coverage or smoke proof for unmatched npm cleanup globs.

options.title: Wait for fresh reporter proof
options.body: Keep the issue waiting on author until there is current evidence that a supported installer path still fails.

recommendation.title: Retire or redirect legacy zsh usage
recommendation.body: Point `molt.bot` users to `https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash` and current ClawHub/OpenClaw install docs, then treat zsh-piped legacy failures as unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen owns the nearest visible ClawHub CLI/package install surface and has already touched adjacent issue triage.
